A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, six figures, Table 1, equations, and Appendices A–I. The supplied material supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original learning-dynamics simulations in Figures 1–2 and 4–6, plus MNIST binary-classification experiments and data analysis in Figure 3 and Table 1.

after.justification: V2 retains these original simulations, MNIST experiments, and data-analysis results, including those in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The common network formulation, gradient-flow training procedure, and linear, quadratic, convolutional, and attention models are unchanged. The revised opening introduces no new algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic learning tasks, in-context linear regression, and MNIST digit-pair classification. Appendix B retains the same activation-function, deep-network, and skip-connection scenarios.

E2.justification: The architecture comparisons and the no-skip, skip-one-layer, and skip-two-layer controls retain the same membership. Newly cited papers are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Experimental settings in the figure captions and Appendix I are unchanged. For example, both MNIST experiments specify width 1000, batch size 64, learning rate 0.01, and initialization variance 10^-12. No evaluation procedure or metric is revised.

E4.justification: Figure 2 retains the same analyses of width, data spectrum, initialization structure, and initialization scale. Appendix B retains the activation-function, depth, and skip-connection analyses without adding or removing a tested question.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed identifiers, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for these experiments. The descriptions of random initialization remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The learning curves, weight configurations, and reported findings in Figures 1–6 are retained. Every Table 1 value is unchanged; for example, the MNIST 3/5 pair has plateau-governing singular values 4.62 and 1.38 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical statements, assumptions, equations, and derivations in Sections 2–5 and Appendices D–H are unchanged. V2 corrects references to Proposition 5 and Lemma 6, which already carried those labels in v1; these are reference corrections rather than theoretical revisions.

C1.justification: The unified explanation of dynamical simplicity through embedded saddles, invariant manifolds, and timescale separation remains intact. V2 foregrounds data-induced low-rank versus initialization-induced sparse weights, but these mechanisms and weight patterns were already described in v1, particularly Section 5 and Appendix C.

C2.justification: The explanations of plateau formation, architectural differences, and distributed versus localized features remain the same. The limitations concerning general deep-network dynamics, exhaustive fixed-point characterization, and rigorous trajectory guarantees are also retained.

D1.justification: Appendix I retains the same data-generation instructions, model dimensions, sample counts, learning rates, initialization scales, and PyTorch convolution example. The supplementary-video link is unchanged, with no new code or data access information.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Berthier (2026), Edelman et al. (2024), Karkada et al. (2025), Teney et al. (2024), Varre et al. (2025), and Wang and Pehlevan (2025). These modestly expand the literature context while retaining the existing contribution positioning.

P1.justification: Parts of the abstract, introduction, and Appendix A are rewritten to emphasize the two timescale mechanisms. V2 also corrects internal result labels, replaces several 'Section' references with 'Appendix', and adds correspondence information. The section and appendix organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adopts ICLR conference headers, different title and heading typography, and revised spacing. Figure 1 has modest panel-alignment and sizing adjustments. All six figures and Table 1 remain, with unchanged substantive contents.

improvement.justification: V2 explains the existing data-versus-initialization distinction more clearly in its opening, broadens the literature context, and corrects several internal references. These provide a modest improvement in clarity and navigation. The underlying theory, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
